newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The House committee on ways and means yesterday buckled under the combined pressures from the Senate and the Department of Finance to lower the proposed 184,000 peso threshold tax exemption for a family of six. (BUSINESSWORLD/CHRONICLE/JOURNAL)
- President Ramos marks his 69th birthday today by launching a massive programme to build 218 bridges in 70 provinces at a total cost of 14 billion pesos. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Defense Secretary Renato de Villa said yesterday he is sure President Ramos will step down from his office when his term ends in June 1998. (STAR)
- The Philippines and the United States have reached agreement on a dispute over rules governing U.S.-bound garment and textile products, a trade official said yesterday. (BULLETIN/STAR)

- The bellwether 91-day Treasury bill rate fell to a single-digit level of 9.804 percent during yesterday's auction from 10.159 percent last week after the Central Bank cut its key overnight borrowing rate last Friday by 0.25 percentage point to 10 percent. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Philippines and Japan signed yesterday in Tokyo agreements on 14 official development assistance projects amounting to 124.28 billion yen. (CHRONICLE/TIMES/TODAY)
